title: Baseten's delta weight sync: decoding zstd commands, GPU as the parent
focus:
Audience: inference-infrastructure engineers who know vLLM/SGLang serving, tensor and expert parallelism, KV cache, and the basic idea of RL weight sync (a trainer publishes new weights every step; rollout engines must load them). Skip explaining RL itself. A previous episode surveyed delta weight sync across frameworks; this one is specifically Baseten's two engineering posts, in order, as one story.

Cover, in this order:
1. Setup: trainer publishes zstd(parent XOR new) deltas to object storage; independent rollout clusters pull and apply. XOR is byte-level, not numeric subtraction. GLM-5.3 numbers: 0.09% of elements change, 716.56 GiB of XOR data compresses to 1.55 GiB.
2. Post 1, why ordinary zstd decoding does too much work: the 16 MB buffer decode-scan-XOR loop still produces and scans all 716 GiB; block headers don't help (128 KiB blocks, nearly all contain a change).
3. Post 1, reading zstd commands directly: literals and sequences (literal length, match length, offset); logical cursor, skip zero matches, record non-zero literals, and handle matches that copy non-zero values (the subtle correctness point).
4. Post 1, GPU apply: absolute values, not XOR, for retry safety; mapping changes into vLLM's fused layout and batching per destination; pause 12 s to 6 s on 8xB300; 36 s publish to first new-policy response; CPU parent copy promoted in 45 s afterwards.
5. Post 2, the CPU copy was the bottleneck: ~770 GB host RAM, KV cache squeezed from 1.1 TB to 275 GB, 45 s promotion, two sources of truth.
6. Post 2, the GPU is the parent: verify at startup, per-tensor Adler-32, keep only (position, XOR mask), gather old values on GPU, verify, stage write plan. Adler-32 updated in O(1) per changed byte; up to 2.3x faster (Kimi K3 30 GB delta, ~230 s to ~100 s).
7. Post 2, sub-second pause (0.8 s on GLM-5.3), per-GPU decoding under TP/EP, separate CUDA-free helper process to avoid the SGLang scheduler's GIL, pipelined download/decode; Kimi K3 1.7 TB on two GB300 nodes, 75 s, 4.1 s pause; freed host RAM used for KV offload (150k-token prefix reload 0.48 s vs 4.9 s prefill; hit rate 2% to 92%, 3.2x throughput per GPU at concurrency 48).

Rules: only state numbers the sources state, and attribute them to Baseten's own measurements. No hype. Do not read URLs aloud. End with a concrete two-sentence recap of the two ideas (decode from zstd commands; GPU as the parent), not a rhetorical question.

CORRECTION for this take: the pause reduction from about 12 s to 6 s on 8xB300 came from the GPU apply step (translating each change to its location in vLLM's fused GPU layout, grouping changes by destination, reading the next shard in parallel and caching the layout translation), NOT from the custom zstd decoder. The decoder's job is avoiding the 716 GiB dense decode; say that separately. Keep everything else as accurate as before.

EXACT FACTS, say them exactly: the hardware for GLM-5.3 is "eight B300 GPUs" (B300, never V100). Publish-to-first-new-policy-response is "about 36 seconds" (not 36.6), and it is the whole pipeline's end-to-end time, not the result of any single step.
ENDING: finish with the two-sentence recap and stop. Do not add any closing speculation or question about future architectures.

- take2 (5:37): fixed the pause attribution, but introduced new errors (confirmed with the medium model): "8 by V100" instead of 8xB300, "36.6 seconds" instead of 36, implies the GPU-apply work produced the 36 s end-to-end figure, and ends on a speculative question about bypassing object storage. Worse than take1.
